subject: Request: Approval for sign-on bonus + accelerated vesting — Sr Backend (EMEA)
messages:
From: Ethan Shah <ethan.shah@talentbridge.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, markus_klein@redwoodai.com
Date: Sat, 7 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Candidate update: Lina Müller — request for comp exception

Hi Priya,

Quick context: Lina (resume attached) is the top candidate for our Sr Backend Engineer (EMEA) role. She has a competing written offer from a marketplace startup in Berlin that is 25% higher on base and includes a sign-on. Candidate is excited about Redwood’s mission and the serving runtime direction, but comp is the blocker.

Recruit asks / proposal from hiring team (requested by recruiter):
- Base: €145,000 (above band midpoint; role band max is €135,000) — we are requesting an out-of-band base approval of +€10k.
- Sign-on: €25,000 (one-time, split over first 6 months)
- Equity refresh: front-loaded 25% of first-year grant as accelerated vesting (to help retention vs. counteroffer)

Why this is time-sensitive: candidate has to respond to the other offer by 2026-02-13. Hiring manager (Matteo) believes Lina is uniquely qualified — 10+ years backend infra, prior work on KV caching and high-throughput systems. She has strong references and would shorten ramp for the inference runtime team.

Attachments: candidate_resume_LinaMueller.pdf, offer_summary.pdf

Can you advise on escalation path and whether comp committee / Markus would consider the +€10k and the one-time sign-on + accelerated vesting? If approved, we can present an updated offer and close before the deadline.

Thanks,
Ethan
TalentBridge (external recruiter)

---
Ethan Shah
Senior Tech Recruiter
E: ethan.shah@talentbridge.com
T: +44 20 5555 1212
From: priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com
To: markus_klein@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
Cc: ethan.shah@talentbridge.com
Date: Sun, 8 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Candidate update: Lina Müller — request for comp exception

Team — forwarding Ethan's note. Quick recommendation from my side: approve the one-time sign-on and the accelerated vesting, and consider the +€10k base as a final flex if we cannot get Lina to accept with sign-on + equity sweetener. Rationale:
- Role urgency: replacing a senior backend will materially unblock critical infra tasks for Q2.
- Cost tradeoff: sign-on + accelerated vesting is more cost-effective over 3 years than raising base.
- Precedent: we did a similar sign-on + 1st-year acceleration for two hires in 2025 (different region) — candidate retention improved and immediate budget delta was manageable.

Please confirm next steps. If Markus wants, I can capture expected run-rate impact in comp_model_2026.xlsx and route to compensation committee. Laura — can you confirm whether accelerated vesting (25% front-load year 1) is HR-compliant for EMEA and whether there are any tax/reporting implications we should flag to the candidate?

Thanks — Priya
Director, Talent Acquisitions
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwoodai.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com, ethan.shah@talentbridge.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Candidate update: Lina Müller — request for comp exception

Thanks for the background. A few questions before I can greenlight anything:
1) Please send the modeled 3-year cash and equity run-rate impact (including payroll taxes) — I need to see the incremental OTE and how this compares to band-overrides we've approved previously.
2) Has the hiring manager exhausted other levers (flexible start date, relocation assistance, discretionary learning stipend)? I want to ensure we’re not over-indexing on cash.
3) Any counteroffer history from Lina's current employer? If she prefers a retention payment, we should structure accordingly.

Priya — please attach comp_model_2026.xlsx with the scenarios. Marissa — I want the hiring manager to document the business risk if we miss this hire (short bullet doc).

If we can see the numbers by EOD Thursday (2026-02-12) I can convene the ad-hoc comp call Friday morning and make a decision.

— Markus
VP, Total Rewards
From: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
To: markus_klein@redwoodai.com, priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Cc: ethan.shah@talentbridge.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Candidate update: Lina Müller — request for comp exception

Markus / Priya / Marissa — I reviewed the facts and the attached comp_model_2026.xlsx (see sheet: scenarios). HR/legal are comfortable with a one-time sign-on of €25,000 (paid in two installments across first 6 months) plus an equity structure that front-loads 25% of the FY1 grant to vest at 6 months (remaining vesting schedule normal thereafter). This solution addresses Lina's immediate counteroffer concern without permanently increasing comp run-rate.

I also reviewed tax considerations for EMEA; we recommend communicating gross vs net sign-on figures to Lina and offering an option for tax-withholding assistance (one-time advisory payment up to €1,200) handled through payroll. Please note:
- We should avoid increasing base above band unless absolutely necessary; approving +€10k base would require written sign-off from the CFO.
- The accelerated equity must be documented in the offer addendum; I'll draft language and route for signature if Markus approves the cash portion.

Marissa — if hiring manager Matteo confirms business impact doc, and Markus signs off on the cash delta after reviewing comp_model_2026.xlsx, HR can finalize offer addendum and we can aim to send candidate updated offer by EOD 2026-02-12 to meet her deadline.

Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: comp_model_2026.xlsx (scenarios tab)
